newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals seek clearer direction.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals seek clearer direction.

text.p: Precious metals dealers were looking for a more settled direction in their markets on Friday after two days of whipsaw movements.

But light selling after New York opened took prices a few points lower across the board lagrely reversing Thursday's silver-led rally, sparked when the dollar slipped against the yen and brought losses on the stock and bond markets.
The silver rally, which was driven by the investment funds, had begun to lose its way on Friday morning after gold showed inability to match it, dealers said.
"Silver hit a brick wall when it got no encouragement from gold. It's been a bit disappointing," a dealer said.
Until New York opened lower, the markets marked time. "Its been bearish for so long everybody kept saying "there is not reason for it to go higher'," another dealer said.
"It (gold) looks pretty good around $378," the dealer added.
Gold was fixed at $378.15 after $378.35 this morning and compared with $378.60 on Thursday afternoon.
The Comex December contract was down $0.70 at $378.90.
Producer selling from Australia in significant volume kept gold's attempts to rise capped in Asia.
"There has been no obvious direction this week, with selling one day and buying the next. We need a good close to set the market up positively for next week," a dealer said.
That would mean a close above $380.00 the dealer said.
But a surge in price was unlikely with market attention focusing on the expiry of the December Comex traded gold and silver option contracts later today, dealers said.
An option gives its owner the right but not the obligation to buy or sell a commodity at a given price on a future date.
Silver was indicated at $4.79/$4.81 unchanged cent after reaching a $4.86 highest bid of the day earlier.
"The (US) funds were the buyers yesterday and there was some short covering but Europe did more of the selling and was caught a bit on the hop," one dealer said.
He added that a falure by silver to close above $4.90 could be taken as a signal to start selling again.
"It could head back lower. The $4.75 is pivotal. If it gets down there again we could see $4.60," the dealer said.
Platinum and palladium were steady at $381.55/$382.55 and $116.00/$117.00, down $0.50 and unchanged respectively.
